summary: King County, WA 20' L-4 tower (1934) replaced an early-1930s cabin; WWII Aircraft Warning post; removed in the 1950s; footings and timber remain per undated guide photos; trail access.

facts.design: 20-foot L-4 tower (1934) replacing an early-1930s cabin; garage built 1940 by CCC Camp F-85
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1950s per sources; the guide's photo captions name footings and old tower timber and bolts, undated

staffing.status: Aircraft Warning Service spotting post used year-round in WWII; activation 1942; end date 1943 or 1944 (sources differ)

access.note: About a mile hike from the Middle Fork Snoqualmie trailhead off the valley road from North Bend; WillhiteWeb mentions no gate or permit; land status not stated in these sources

visit.trail_note: Drive the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Valley Road from North Bend to the Middle Fork Trailhead, then the CCC Trail and an old switchback trail, about 500 feet of gain

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest)

events.note: Cabin built in the early 1930s per Register and WillhiteWeb (Kresek inventory); no exact year in sources, 1930 is a placeholder
20-foot L-4 tower built, replacing the cabin
Panorama photographs taken August 1, 1934 (Forest Lookouts; WillhiteWeb captions)
Garage constructed by CCC Camp F-85 (WillhiteWeb); 1940 letter quoted on Forest Lookouts describes plans to build it
Aircraft Warning Service post activated September 4, 1942, Seattle Filter Center (Forest Lookouts); used year-round in WWII (WillhiteWeb)
Forest Lookouts: deactivated October 16, 1943 (conflicts with 1944 caption)
WillhiteWeb photo caption: May 1, 1944 A.W.S. document showing inactivation date
Removed in the 1950s per all sources; no exact year given, 1950 is a placeholder
Registered April 24, 2012 as US 1253, WA 153; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: cabin in early 1930s; replaced 1934 with 20' L-4 tower; tower removed in 1950s
evidence.quote: The first lookout on this site was a cabin built in the early 1930s. That was replaced in 1934 with a 20' L-4 tower, which was removed in the 1950s.

evidence.supports: location 11 miles northeast of North Bend

evidence.quote: a 20' L-4 tower was built in 1934

evidence.supports: cabin placed on site in early 1930s per Kresek inventory

A few years later, during WWII, the lookout was used year-round as an aircraft spotting station.

corrections.proposed: Remove. Nordrum is US 1253, WA 153 and Nooksack is US 1252, WA 152, so they do not share a number.
corrections.why: Register entries differ: Nordrum US 1253, WA 153 (this source); Nooksack US 1252, WA 152 (firetower.org/lookouts/us/wa/nooksack-lookout-site/)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives deactivation on October 16, 1943; a WillhiteWeb photo caption cites a May 1, 1944 document showing the inactivation date. Not reconciled; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 'conflicts' entry is wrong: the register numbers differ (US 1253 here, US 1252 for Nooksack), see corrections. Cabin and removal dates are given only as decades, so the events use placeholder years 1930 and 1950 and say so in the notes. Access rated public from WillhiteWeb's directions; no gate or permit is mentioned and land status is not stated in the sources read. The footing and timber captions are undated. One WebSearch was run; a Wikipedia background snippet was not cited. Page reads used: 5.
